EspFace.title: EspFace
EspFace.intro: `EspFace face;` is the facade a sketch talks to: lifecycle, identity, security, transports, system features and value updates. Builder calls go through `face.ui()` (see [Ui](/reference/ui)). Every setter returns `EspFace&` so calls chain.

Ui.title: Ui builder
Ui.intro: `face.ui()` returns the default `Ui`; `face.addUi("setup")` creates another one that a transport can serve instead. Builder methods return a [WidgetRef](/reference/widgetref) for chaining; widgets declared after `page()` belong to that page. The tables below are the overview from the firmware README; the sections that follow list every method.

WidgetRef.title: WidgetRef
WidgetRef.intro: The chainable handle every builder call returns. All methods return `WidgetRef&`; the reference stays valid for the lifetime of the `Ui` (widgets are never removed).

PropRef.title: PropRef
PropRef.intro: Runtime prop updates without a rebuild: `ui.prop("temp").label("Boiler temp").color("#f00");` collects the changes and sends one `prop` message to all clients when the temporary `PropRef` goes out of scope (end of the statement). The firmware keeps mutable props so a later `ui` resend is consistent.

groups.EspFace::Lifecycle: Call `begin()` once in `setup()` after the identity setters; then either pump `loop()` yourself or start the networking task.
groups.EspFace::Transports: The WebSocket server is on by default; the other transports are added by one call each and share the session logic (PIN, tokens, `ESPFACE_MAX_CLIENTS`).
groups.EspFace::Values and events: Shortcuts for the most common runtime calls of the default UI (`face.ui()`); they return `false` when the id is unknown or the value is invalid.
groups.Ui::Builder: Each call appends one widget; ids must match `^[A-Za-z0-9_]{1,15}$` and be unique within the UI. A `group`, `page` or `row` must be declared before the widgets that reference it.
groups.WidgetRef::Callbacks and bindings: Callbacks run inside `face.loop()` (or the networking task) when a client sends `set`/`ev`; keep them short.

EspFace::EspFace.desc: Constructs the facade; nothing starts until `begin()`.

EspFace::begin.desc: Starts the library: device id from the MAC, NVS namespace `espface`, mDNS/AP name derived from `name`, restores persisted values, starts the enabled transports. Call once in `setup()`.

args.name: display name shown by the clients and used for the mDNS host and the AP SSID

EspFace::loop.desc: Pumps transports, sessions, the 100 ms value flush, dialogs, OTA and NTP. Call from `loop()` unless `beginTask()` runs it on its own FreeRTOS task.

EspFace::beginTask.desc: Runs `loop()` on a dedicated FreeRTOS task so the sketch's `loop()` may block.
EspFace::beginTask.example:
face.beginTask();          // defaults: 8 KB stack, priority 1, any core
face.beginTask(12288, 2, 1);

EspFace::delay.desc: Like `delay(ms)` but keeps calling `loop()` so clients stay served while the sketch waits.

EspFace::setPin.desc: Enables PIN pairing (HMAC-SHA256 challenge-response, cap `pin`). The PIN is stored in NVS; a client can change it later with `sys pin.set`, which wins over the sketch value unless `force` is true. `nullptr` or an empty string disables the PIN.

args.force: overwrite a PIN a client set at runtime

EspFace::setProject.desc: Project/group name shown in the device list of the clients (`proj` in hello and mDNS TXT).

EspFace::setIcon.desc: Icon name from the shared set for the device list.

EspFace::setVersion.desc: Firmware version string (`fw` in hello and info; compared with GitHub releases when `setRepo` is set).

EspFace::setRepo.desc: GitHub `owner/repo`; lets clients offer a user-triggered release check and `ota.url` install.

EspFace::setAbout.desc: Free text shown on the info page.

EspFace::setPort.desc: HTTP/WebSocket port (default 80; falls back to 8080 when the bind fails and logs it). Call before `begin()`.

EspFace::enableWs.desc: `false` before `begin()` skips the http/WebSocket server entirely (BLE-only or serial-only devices).

EspFace::logTo.desc: Where library log lines go (default `Serial`). Pass `nullptr` when the UI runs over `Serial` so log lines stay off the wire.

EspFace::setRendererHost.desc: Origin the bootstrap page loads `/r/1/app.js` from; compile-time default `ESPFACE_RENDERER_HOST`. Use it when hosting your own renderer.

EspFace::enableOta.desc: Adds caps `ota` and `otaurl`: OTA push over WebSocket binary frames, `ota.url` download and `POST /update`. The Update/HTTPClient/TLS code is only linked when a sketch calls this.

EspFace::setOtaCaCert.desc: PEM CA certificate used to verify https for `ota.url` downloads and ntfy. Without it https is used unverified.
EspFace::setOtaCaCert.example:
static const char CA_CERT[] PROGMEM = "-----BEGIN CERTIFICATE-----\n...";
face.setOtaCaCert(CA_CERT);

EspFace::enableNtp.desc: IDF SNTP client; the system time feeds `face.time()` and the clock widgets (cap `ntp`). `tz` is a POSIX TZ string or nullptr for UTC.

EspFace::ntfy.desc: Configures direct ntfy notifications (cap `ntfy`); `notify()` then POSTs from the device on its own task. `token` is an optional bearer token.

EspFace::ntfyRateLimit.desc: Minimum interval between notifications (default 10 000 ms); extra messages queue (4 slots) or are dropped.
EspFace::ntfyRateLimit.example: face.ntfyRateLimit(60000);   // at most one per minute

EspFace::notify.desc: Queues a notification; returns false when ntfy is not configured or the queue is full.

EspFace::addUi.desc: Creates a second, independent UI that a transport can serve with `transport.use(ui)`; e.g. an open setup UI on BLE next to the main UI on WiFi (`Provisioning` example).

EspFace::wifi.example:
face.wifi().autoConnect();          // stored credentials, else captive AP espFace-<id>
face.wifi().setApPassword("setup123");

EspFace::ws.desc: The WebSocket/http transport object (port, renderer host, `running()`).

EspFace::serial.desc: Adds any Arduino `Stream` (UART, USB CDC, `BluetoothSerial`) as a one-client line transport. Returns the transport for `setIdleTimeout(ms)` / `use(ui)`.

EspFace::ble.desc: Enables the NimBLE transport (build with `-DESPFACE_BLE`); returns it for `setName()` / `use(ui)`.

EspFace::btClassic.desc: Enables Bluetooth Classic SPP (build with `-DESPFACE_BT_CLASSIC`, classic ESP32 only, exclusive with BLE).

EspFace::core.desc: The protocol core (sessions, caps, hooks). Rarely needed by sketches.

EspFace::set.desc: Updates a widget value and pushes it to the clients (coalesced into one `upd` every 100 ms). Overloads for bool, float/double, int, uint32_t (colors, flags), strings and the joystick pair.

EspFace::setRows.desc: Table rows as a raw JSON array of rows.

EspFace::setPoints.desc: Map points as a raw JSON array of `[lat, lon, label]`.

EspFace::push.desc: Appends a chart point (timestamp: unix ms when the time is known, else uptime ms).

EspFace::log.desc: Sends a log line: without a widget id to the console view of the clients, with an id to that `log` widget (optionally colored).

EspFace::toast.desc: Transient message on all clients; `lvl` is `info`, `warn` or `err`.

EspFace::time.desc: Unix seconds from NTP, else from the last client `time` message, else 0.

EspFace::setTime.desc: Feeds an authoritative time (e.g. from an RTC).

EspFace::onConnect.desc: Called when a client finished the handshake (`ClientInfo`: slot, transport name, isWeb).
EspFace::onConnect.example: face.onConnect([](const ClientInfo& c) { Serial.printf("client on %s\n", c.transport); });

EspFace::onReboot.desc: Called right before a client-, OTA- or sketch-triggered reboot (`RebootReason::Client`, `Ota`, `Sketch`).

EspFace::reboot.desc: Reboots after `delayMs` (clients are told first, `onReboot` runs).

EspFace::id.desc: Device id (6 to 12 lowercase hex from the MAC).

Ui::name.desc: The UI's name (`main` for the default one).

Ui::pin.desc: Overrides the device PIN for this UI: `""` makes it open, any string sets its own PIN; without a call the global `face.setPin()` applies.

Ui::page.desc: Starts a page (tab / bottom-nav entry); widgets declared afterwards belong to it until the next `page()`.

Ui::group.desc: Group card; widgets join it with `.group(id)`. `.fold()` makes it collapsible.

Ui::row.desc: Row; widgets join it with `.row(id).size(w)` and sit side by side with relative widths.

Ui::spacer.desc: Empty space with relative width `w` and height `h` px.

Ui::label.desc: Read-only text or number; `.fmt("%.1f")` formats numbers.

Ui::button.desc: Button; `onClick` for a press, `.hold()` + `onEvent` for press (1) and release (0).
Ui::button.example:
ui.button("reset", "Reset error").hint("Clears the error latch").onClick([] { err = 0; });
ui.button("horn", "Horn").hold().onEvent([](int v) { digitalWrite(HORN, v); });

Ui::sw.desc: Switch (bool); `.labels(on, off)` sets state labels, `.icon()` without a label gives an icon-only toggle.

Ui::slider.desc: Slider (float) with range, step and unit.

Ui::text.desc: Single-line text input; `.secret()` masks it, `.regex()` validates client-side.

Ui::select.desc: Dropdown (value = option index); `.style("seg")` renders segmented buttons.

Ui::progress.desc: Bar (output); `.center()` draws a bipolar bar from the middle.

Ui::led.desc: Indicator (bool); `.rgb()` makes the value a 0xRRGGBB color.

Ui::chart.desc: Live chart with a client-side ring buffer of `winSeconds`; add series with `.series(id, lbl, color)`, feed with `face.push()`.

Ui::textblock.example: ui.textblock("help", "Set the target and enable the pump.\nThe horn button is momentary.");

Ui::log.desc: Log view with a client ring buffer of `cap` lines and `rows` visible lines; feed with `face.log(id, msg, color)`. `ESPFACE_LOG_HISTORY` lines are replayed on connect.

Ui::flags.desc: Checkbox set; the value is a bitmask (bit i = option i, max 32).

Ui::joystick.desc: Joystick; `.center()` auto-returns, `.exp()` exponential response; `onMove(x, y)` each -100..100.
Ui::joystick.example: ui.joystick("joy", "Valve").center().square().onMove([](int x, int y) { drive(x, y); });

Ui::dpad.desc: Direction pad; `onEvent` gets 'u', 'd', 'l', 'r', 'c' on press and 0 on release.
Ui::dpad.example: ui.dpad("pad", "Move").onEvent([](int k) { if (k == 'u') forward(); if (k == 0) stop(); });

Ui::table.desc: Table (output); add at least one `.column(lbl, w, align)`, fill with `face.setRows()`.

Ui::image.desc: Image from a URL the client can reach; change it with `ui.prop(id).src(url)`.

Ui::clock.desc: Clock (output); the library pushes the device time every minute and the client ticks locally. `fmt` tokens: YYYY MM DD HH mm ss.

Ui::map.desc: Map (output, online tiles in the clients); fill with `face.setPoints()`.

Ui::add.desc: Any widget type without the convenience defaults (e.g. for props set entirely by chain calls).

Ui::set.desc: Updates a value from the sketch and pushes it (same as `face.set()`); returns false for unknown ids or invalid values.

Ui::setRows.desc: Table rows as a raw JSON array.

Ui::setPoints.desc: Map points as a raw JSON array.

Ui::tickClocks.desc: Pushes `unix` to every clock widget; the core calls it every minute, sketches rarely need it.

Ui::get.desc: Current value of a widget (nullptr when unknown).
Ui::get.example:
const Value* v = face.ui().get("target");
if (v) target = v->asFloat();

Ui::prop.desc: Starts a runtime prop update (see [PropRef](/reference/propref)); sent when the statement ends.

Ui::show.desc: Hides or shows a widget (`vis` prop).

Ui::rebuild.desc: Bumps `rev` and resends the whole UI to all clients after structural changes (new widgets added at runtime).

Ui::confirm.desc: Opens a confirm dialog on every client; the first answer wins, others are dismissed; without an answer the callback gets `ok = false` after `timeoutS`.
Ui::confirm.example: face.ui().confirm("d1", "Shut down the pump?", [](bool ok, const Str&) { if (ok) digitalWrite(PUMP, 0); });

Ui::prompt.desc: Opens a text prompt on every client; the callback gets the typed text.
Ui::prompt.example: face.ui().prompt("d2", "New device name", [](bool ok, const Str& text) { if (ok) rename(text); }, "Boiler");

Ui::push.desc: Appends a chart point; `tsMs` 0 = now (unix ms when known, else uptime ms).

Ui::logLine.desc: Log line to a log widget (`logId`), or to the clients' console view when `logId` is nullptr.

WidgetRef::group.desc: Puts the widget into a group card declared earlier with `ui.group()`.

WidgetRef::page.desc: Puts the widget on a page (default: the page declared last, else the first).

WidgetRef::row.desc: Puts the widget into a row declared earlier with `ui.row()`.

WidgetRef::size.desc: Relative width inside a row (default 1) and an optional fixed height in px.

WidgetRef::hint.desc: Help text shown on long-press / hover.

WidgetRef::icon.desc: Icon name from the shared set (see [Icons](/guide/icons)).

WidgetRef::color.desc: Accent color `#rrggbb` (button, switch, slider, progress, led).

WidgetRef::readOnly.desc: Rendered but not settable (`ro`); `set` from a client is answered with err 7.

WidgetRef::range.desc: Min/max for slider, number, gauge, progress.

WidgetRef::hold.desc: Momentary button: `onEvent` gets 1 on press and 0 on release.

WidgetRef::regex.desc: Client-side validation regex for text inputs.

WidgetRef::style.desc: Style per type: select `list|seg`, gauge `arc|round|linear`, chart `line|bar|area`.

WidgetRef::fmt.desc: printf-style format for label values, or the clock format.

WidgetRef::fold.desc: Collapsible group (state lives in the client).

WidgetRef::values.desc: Chart shows the current value of each series next to the legend.

WidgetRef::rgb.desc: LED whose value is a 0xRRGGBB color instead of a bool.

WidgetRef::zone.desc: Colored range on a gauge; call it once per zone.

WidgetRef::series.desc: Adds a chart series (id used in `face.push()`), with optional label and color.

WidgetRef::column.desc: Adds a table column with relative width and alignment (`left|center|right`).

WidgetRef::maxlen.desc: Maximum length of a text input.

WidgetRef::persist.desc: Stores the input value in NVS on change (debounced) and restores it before `begin()` returns; `onChange` fires once with the restored value. The widget id doubles as the NVS key (15 chars).

WidgetRef::value.desc: Initial value (overridden by a persisted one).

WidgetRef::onChange.desc: Called when a client sets the widget; the lambda's argument type selects the conversion: `bool`, `int`, `uint32_t`, `float`, `double`, `const String&`, `const char*` or `const Value&`.

WidgetRef::onEvent.desc: Raw event: hold buttons get 1/0, dpad gets 'u','d','l','r','c' and 0 on release.

WidgetRef::onMove.example: ui.joystick("joy", "Valve").onMove([](int x, int y) { drive(x, y); });

WidgetRef::bind.desc: Two-way binding to a variable: client changes write it, and `face.loop()` pushes it when the sketch changes it.

PropRef::options.desc: Replaces the options of a select / flags widget.
